text:
Anya: Heads-up: planning an RBAC + egress gateway hardening for on‑prem/private deploys next week. Scope: tighten k8s RBAC on network/egress controllers, deploy an egress gateway (nginx + WireGuard) that only allows traffic to approved proxies, ensure fluent-bit log shipping to S3/SIEM encrypted with customer KMS, and update vuln triage + incident runbook. Questions: KMS pattern for airgapped customers? Any blockers on log agent ports? Volunteers for rollout runbook?
Mike: +1. Curious about KMS — customers want CMK in their HSM (onprem). We should support envelope encryption so fluent-bit writes encrypted blobs and S3 only stores ciphertext.
Jules: For airgapped installs we usually do envelope + local KMS shim (Vault auto‑unseal w/ HSM) — teams can bring their own CMK or we can accept a wrapped data key during install.
Ops-Jen: Log agent ports: fluent-bit needs outbound to our s3/proxy endpoints or to an onprem collector. If we enforce egress gateway, make sure the kube-proxy/netpol allow the agent to reach the gateway on TCP/443 or 8443. Some customers run fluentd on 24224 — we should avoid forcing new ports.
SecurityBot: Quick vuln triage note: CVE-2025-3341 found in alpine base used by egress-proxy image (privileged netutil lib). Patch recommended. See internal vuln tracker #VULN-2241.
Anya: Good catch. Mike/Jules, can you confirm minimal image patch plan + nonroot user? We must avoid CAP_NET_ADMIN where possible.
Mike: Patch plan: move to debian-slim base, upgrade netutil lib to v2.1.4, add user 'egw' and drop CAP_NET_RAW/CAP_NET_ADMIN. Add e2e tests for fallback policy.
Jules: On the KMS front: recommended pattern for private/onprem: 1) envelope keys generated by agent (data key), 2) data key encrypted by customer CMK via local HSM/Vault transit or AWS KMS (if connected), 3) only ciphertext leaves the tenant. Documented fallback: customer provides pre-wrapped key at install time for airgapped installs.
Kevin: Does our current rollout plan include canary for RBAC changes? We had a prior incident where ServiceAccount token couldn't reach metrics exporter after a narrow RBAC change.
Anya: Yes — plan is staged: dev clusters -> 10% customer canary -> global. Canary includes automated smoke: control-plane health, ingress e2e, fluent-bit log delivery, and a simulated incident drill (rotate key).
Ops-Jen: NetworkPolicy snippet that I've tested (k8s 1.25) — allows egress from fluent-bit namespace to approved proxy CIDR only:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-fluentbit-egress
  namespace: logging
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: fluent-bit
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.240.0/24 # approved proxies
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
Jules: Also add a hostNetwork exception for bootstrap nodes in airgapped installs; otherwise fluent-bit can't reach local collector during bootstrap. Documented in install guide.
Mike: For audit logging: ship two streams — (1) control-plane audit events (k8s audit) and (2) app logs. Both should be signed/timestamped client-side before send. Suggest adding an HMAC of payload with rotating key derived from the data key so SIEM can verify integrity.
Anya: Agree. Add fields: envelope_kms_key_id (customer CMK id), wrapped_data_key_sha256, signature. That helps post‑mortem integrity checks.
SecurityBot: Incident runbook notes: If egress gateway goes down or keys are rotated unexpectedly, runbook step 3 should call: 1) revoke gateway routing, 2) revert to local log retention mode (flush to local disk), 3) alert SOC with signed heartbeat mismatch. Add automation to do step 2 automatically after 2m of failed egress attempts.
Kevin: For RBAC: propose introducing a new ClusterRole 'egress-gateway-controller' with only verbs: get,list,watch,patch on configmaps/secrets, and create/update on NetworkPolicy CRDs — nothing else. No access to PVs.
Anya: +1. Also add a PodSecurityPolicy-esque admission check ensure egress pod does not mount hostPath and runs as nonroot.
Ops-Jen: One edge case: customers using hostPath logging to /var/log may need a preflight to copy/rotate logs before we flip to gateway-only egress. Add a preflight script that scans mounts.
Jules: KMS integration testing plan: 1) simulated HSM via Vault dev 2) wrapped-key install flow (airgap) 3) external KMS (AWS/Azure) connectivity test 4) XKS-style latency tests if using external HSM.
Mike: We should produce a short checklist for SOC: what to look for after rollout — increased 403s from apps (RBAC too tight), missing audit heartbeat signatures, fluent-bit send errors, and kernel denial logs for dropped caps.
Anya: I'll draft the checklist and runbook updates. Volunteers to review: Mike, Jules, Ops-Jen, Kevin?
Mike: happy to review.
Jules: can do the KMS bits.
Ops-Jen: I'll run the network and agent tests.
Kevin: I'll validate RBAC roles and canary gating.
SRE-Bot: deploy-bot: Started canary job 1767032001 for egress-gateway-hardening -> dev (job id: cbg-1767). Logs: https://ci.internal/reports/cbg-1767 
Anya: Thanks. One last question — retention of audit logs in airgap: do we allow local encrypted retention >90 days? Some regulated customers require 7 years. We should document limits and guidance for onprem archival.
Jules: We can support long retention locally (7y) but must warn about storage cost and rotation. Recommended: local encrypted retention + offline tape/archive export.
Anya: Perfect. I'll post the draft runbook + checklist tomorrow. If anything else comes up ping me. :thumbsup:
Mike: small nit — add the literal command to rotate wrapped key in runbook. People love copy/paste.
Anya: Will do. Thanks all.
